Hi team — looping in some concise model-fit guidance / benchmarks Alicia asked for. High level first, then specific next steps we can hand to the eval run.

Recommended models (tradeoffs)
- redwood-emb-md-1536 (proprietary): 1536-dim dense vectors, best overall semantic separation on short product titles and long descriptions. Stronger NDCG / MRR for catalog retrieval in our internal tests.
- sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (768): fast & cheap, good baseline for semantic grouping but lower recall on fine-grained product disambiguation.
- open alternative: SBERT-based 1024-dim variants (good middle ground for storage vs quality).

Key benchmark numbers (approx., on similar retail catalog tasks)
- Baseline (MiniLM 768): recall@10 ~ 0.62, MRR ~ 0.35, top-10 NDCG ~ 0.58
- redwood-emb-md-1536: recall@10 ~ 0.72, MRR ~ 0.48, top-10 NDCG ~ 0.69
- Dimensionality impact: moving 768 -> 1536 typically improves recall by ~8–12 pts on ambiguous short-title queries, at ~2x storage cost.

Drift & monitoring notes
- Observed mean cosine similarity drift is a practical early indicator: on catalogs with frequent new SKUs we see a shift ~0.01–0.03 over 6 months without retrain / reindex.
- Recommend: weekly cohort checks on cosine distributions, plus embedding-mean / pairwise-distance histograms. If mean cosine shifts >0.02 or std dev increases substantially, consider re-embedding affected partitions.
- Dimensional collapse detection: track explained variance via PCA on a sample (watch for drops in cumulative variance explained by top components).

Evaluation harness & prompt sets
- We'll run a 2-week head-to-head on a 500k sample (your export) vs a control set. We'll evaluate recall@K (K=1,5,10), MRR, and latency p50/p95.
- Sample prompt sets attached (sample_prompts.txt). We'll also iterate with a small set of user queries you can flag as high-priority.

Operational recommendations
- Use L2-normalized embeddings + cosine similarity for retrieval. Persist embeddings as float16 or quantized vector store (if storage is a concern) — but validate downstream ANN accuracy (HNSW / Faiss PQ).
- If storage constraints are tight: consider 1024-d compressed variants with periodic full 1536 re-embeds for high-volume SKUs.

Links / artifacts
- Public benchmark overview: https://redwood-inference.com/benchmarks/embeddings/semantic-search-overview.md
- Shared drive with eval notebook & metrics: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xExampleBenchmarkDriveLink
- HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/ACME-42
